accessibility: The page title is the level-1 heading; each Flow row is one pressable target named by the Flow's name.
A problem count is text inside a badge with an icon, so it is never conveyed by color alone.
Rows keep a visible 2px primary focus outline.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Button, Badge, Icon, ListItem, EmptyState); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (Flow names); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
This View models the page content only; the Workbench shell (sidebar, top bar) is shown by the Workbench View.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A person opened the UX Flows destination (/flows) of the Workbench; the page lists the Workspace's Flows and never redirects into one.
The base state lists the dogfood Workspace's two Flows with no problems; Variants add the problem count and the empty states.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the Workbench renders the live page and this View is its design reference.
spec.intent: Show the UX Flows list of the Workbench as built from Adapter Widgets only: every Flow of the Workspace as one row that opens it, with a problem count where the Flow cannot be played, and an empty state that says what a Flow is.
interactionRules: Each row is one pressable target that opens that Flow; its trailing chevron is decoration.
A Flow with validation problems carries a danger badge with the problem count; a Flow without problems carries none.
The New Flow button is offered to a person who can write Flows, on a desktop window only; with no Flows, the empty state offers it instead of the header.
With no Flows the empty state says what a Flow is and names create_flow for agents; a person who cannot write Flows sees the same text without the button.
